data.name: Zaphiel
data.gender_notes: Zaphiel is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew mythology, Zaphiel was considered the angel of the west. He led the armies of God against the forces of darkness. In Christian tradition, he is often identified with the archangel Michael, the prince of the heavenly host. The name Zaphiel carries the meaning “God of the West” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Zaphiel usually hope their child will grow to embody god of the west and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength, courage, and divine protection against darkness.
data.etymology: Zaphiel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of the West.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Zaphiel total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_latin.name: Zaphiel
in_latin.long_meaning: Zaphiel, Angelus Iustitiae, Visio Dei. Zaphiel est nomen angelorum qui apparuerunt Iesu in Monte Tabor. Visio Dei est apparitio divinitatis in forma angelorum.

in_english.name: Zaphiel
in_english.meaning: angel of justice, vision of God, heavenly messenger
in_english.long_meaning: Zaphiel is a name of an angel in the Book of Revelation, and is also used to refer to the angel who appeared to Jesus on Mount Tabor. The name Zaphiel is derived from the Hebrew words 'tzaphi' meaning 'angel' and 'El' meaning 'God'. The name is also associated with the concept of divine justice and the vision of God.

data.cultural_impact: In Greek mythology, the name "Apollo" was associated with the sun, light, knowledge, and prophecy. In Roman mythology, Apollo was synonymous with the Greek god and retained these attributes.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, St. Apollo is not recognized as a saint, but the name "Apollo" has spiritual significance in the sense that it brings to mind the divine attributes associated with the ancient god: the radiance and light of God illuminating our path.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Zaphiel is the name of an angel in Hebrew mythology, meaning "swift in God." He is believed to be the highest-ranking angel in charge of the divine liturgy and the angelic choir in heaven. Zaphiel is a symbol of divine wisdom, swift action, and unwavering devotion to God.

historical_references.reference: According to Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite, an influential early Christian philosopher, Zaphiel is identified as the archangel who leads the celestial hierarchy and presides over the order of thrones.
historical_references.context: In the context of early Christian philosophy and angelology, Pseudo-Dionysius' works were highly influential in shaping the understanding of the celestial hierarchy and the roles of various angels, including Zaphiel.

historical_references.reference: In some Jewish and early Christian texts, Zophar and Zophiel are considered to be the same figure, with Zophar being the name used in Job and Zophiel being the angelic name. Zophar is depicted as a counselor to Job in the Book of Job, urging him to consider the divine justice behind his suffering.
historical_references.context: The name Zophar appears in the Hebrew Bible (Old Testament), while the angelic name Zophiel emerges in some Jewish and early Christian texts. The two names are believed to refer to the same figure, highlighting the evolving understanding of angels and their roles in religious traditions.

In angelology, Zaphiel is known as an archangel, which is a high-ranking angel in various religious traditions. In fantasy role-playing games, Zaphiel is a common character name and is often depicted as a powerful and noble angelic being. In science fiction, Zaphiel is sometimes used as a character name or as a reference to a celestial being. Some popular platforms where these modern usages of Zaphiel can be found include tabletop role-playing games like Dungeons & Dragons, video games like Diablo and World of Warcraft, and literature such as the works of J.R.R. Tolkien and Michael Moorcock.
